digest.component_or_area: plan-review criterion T1 (overlay-priorart); web search capability routing
propositions: T1's declared server-side web-search tool was silently withdrawn during Bedrock cutover because the provider-name prefix gate 'resolved.startswith("anthropic")' no longer matched bedrock-qualified Claude models, leaving T1 to run on model knowledge alone instead of grounded sources.

The web-access decision was made by provider-name prefix matching rather than capability registry membership, violating the epic's zero-exceptions rule that qualification must come from registry membership, not name shape.
The silent withdrawal left no signal in signed verdicts; provider_provenance.capabilities did not record whether web access was attached, making future silent withdrawals undetectable.
Bedrock's Converse API does not expose Anthropic's server-side web_search tool in supported_native_tools, so T1 must be served via a local DuckDuckGo fallback route rather than native web search.

The original provider-side-only design that avoided writing a rebar-side fetch tool must be revisited to support every provider; web access is now required on every provider, not optional or provider-dependent.

A homegrown HTTP fetch capability introduced for the fallback must be bounded on volume, shape, and authority to avoid untrusted-input risks in a blocking criterion, and prompt-injection from fetched content must be handled explicitly.
